items.title: The 'from_short' rule blocks every long topic on this long-first channel
items.detail: generator/topics.py winning_short() requires a long topic to name one of our Shorts with 100+ views in the top third by stayed to watch (a channel #1 rule, owner 2026-11-12). This channel's profile is long-first (a long video a week, Shorts cut from it; longPerWeek 2) and has one Short with 25 views, so all 10 topics in longform/topics.json are blocked and Studio cannot make this week's 2 long videos. Fix: let a channel opt out (e.g. channel.json "longFrom": "feed" or skip the rule when profile is long-first) until it has 3+ Shorts with 100+ views; add a test. Worked when `state --format long` shows usable_now true for the feed's topics.
items.outcome: Fixed by the owner's rule of 2026-11-22: generator/topics.py no longer blocks a long topic on from_short or a Short's views (winning_short removed, on every channel); scripts/guard.py refuses a branch that brings it back. state --format long shows every feed topic usable.

items.title: Long titles: a question or 'inside / what happens', no figure
items.detail: Niche scan 18 Nov, long videos 7-25 min (n=216): titles with a question mark hit 3x their channel's median 23% of the time vs 10% without; 'inside / what happens' titles 24% (median 1.41x, n=17); a digit in the title 10% vs 15%. Studio: phrase the title as the question people search, keep the figure for the thumbnail or the hook. Judge on the long test once 4 long videos are out.

items.title: Our 7-8 minute band sits in the niche's weakest length
items.detail: Niche scan: 360-600 s long videos hit 4% of the time (median 1,352 views) vs 19% at 600-900 s. The owner capped long videos at 8 minutes for render time (channel.json, 2026-11-18). Owner's call; revisit when render time allows 10-12 minutes.

items.title: Build each long video as a walk through one object, a viewer question opening every chapter
items.detail: Our only breakout, the Crossrail Short (v-20261122-21, 1,362 views vs 284 for our next best; its stayed-to-watch is not in yet), walks one machine front to back: wheel, chamber, conveyor, erector, rams, each beat opened by the question a viewer would ask ('How?', 'Why doesn't the ground cave in?', 'Where does it go?'). Studio: order long chapters along the object's physical path (front to back, outside in, top down), open each chapter on that question in the viewer's voice, and put the causal step (the profile's 'never skip it') in its own chapter. Worked if the first long video's retention curve has no chapter-boundary cliff deeper than 10 points (stats.yml drop points).

items.title: Title on one moment of an everyday action ('in one second', 'when you tap')
items.detail: Niche scan 18 Nov, long videos 7-25 min (n=215): titles framed on one moment or the viewer's action ('in one second', 'one frame', 'when you ...') hit 3x their channel's median 2 of 4 times (median 10x; Silicon Up Close's CPU and AI-chip videos) vs 13% for the rest. Small sample: fold into the open tech-long-title-question experiment as its second arm rather than adopting.

items.title: A long format for machines and megaprojects ('how it's built / how the machine works')
items.detail: The channel's long formats (inside_when_you, how_ai_works, how_network_works) have no home for a machine or a build. 2+ videos over 1M share that shape: 'Inside Virginia's $4 Billion Tunneling Megaproject' (BuildWitt, 3.0M), 'The Real Reason Starship Has 33 Engines' (The Space Race, 2.1M), 'MEGA TUNNEL MACHINES' (WELT, 1.8M), 'Inside SpaceX's $3 Billion Starfactory' (1.2M). Improver: add a long format 'how_the_machine_works' (tier core) to channels/how-tech-and-ai-actually-work-chips-ai-p/research/formats.json: the machine's job and one impossible constraint in the hook, a front-to-back walk of its parts, the constraint solved last. The rocket and Crossrail topics are filed under inside_when_you until then.

items.title: 3D long videos: dark stages read as 'empty' to the craft gate; give every place texture
items.detail: L-20261123-21 (Starlink) failed the empty-frame gate twice (51, then 16 of 85 stills) on smooth night skies, space and plain walls. What passed: a field of soft glowing motes in every place (Dust), surface detail (pegboard, panelling, floorboards, a lat/long grid on the Earth, a measuring grid on glass), and cameras framed on things, not sky. The improver could lift Dust, DotGrid and Lines from remotion/src/videos/L-20261123-21/kit.tsx into remotion/src/three/.

items.title: A 7-minute 3D long video takes about 7 hours to render in the cloud
items.detail: L-20261123-21 (426 s, 11 chunks of 1,200 frames, swangle software GL on 4 cores) rendered 05:18-12:04 UTC, 27-74 min a chunk; the bench chunk was slowest (materials created per frame with continuous opacity: quantise them). Plan the run's time around it, and keep per-frame materials cached (q()).

items.title: Scout feed fact: Starlink altitude 550 km was out of date
items.detail: The fact review found SpaceX is lowering its ~4,400 satellites from 550 km to about 480 km during 2026 (Space.com, 1 Jan 2026). Studio corrected 2026-11-18-starlink-flat-dish in longform/topics.json. The same topic's copy in research/topics.json (research's lane) still says 550 km. Scout: check as_of figures against the last year's news before putting them in a topic.

items.title: Directed 3D beats need a camera key every ~1.5 s, and fast anchor hops leave empty frames
items.detail: L-20261124-21: the 1.8 s picture-gap rule (channel motion.maxGapSec) meant ~100 extra camera keys, added on spoken words with the estimated voice. QA then caught three stills where the camera was mid-move between far anchors (benches, cutaway, phone), looking at a wall. Keep the filler keys on the same anchor, and avoid close shots on a different anchor less than ~1 s after the last move. The improver could build the filler into a lint helper.
items.reason: director.md: extra keys for the picture gap go at the same size (a pan or orbit) or as moments, never a size change, and no close shot on another anchor within ~1 s of the last move; the new camera gate (renderer/craft.py camera_problems) enforces the size side. 2026-11-24

items.title: Label3D pins a label whose anchor is off screen to the top-left corner, over the logo
items.detail: L-20261124-21 QA round 1: eight labels piled into the top-left corner on close shots, on the logo and the NOT TO SCALE badge. Studio worked around it (labels end after 48 frames, the worst labels dropped). The improver could hide a Label3D when its point is outside the frame instead of clamping it (remotion/src/three/Label3D.tsx, clampShift).
items.reason: remotion/src/three/Label3D.tsx: a label whose point is off screen hides instead of being clamped into the corner. 2026-11-24

items.title: The estimated voice runs ~14% short of Kokoro on this channel's long videos
items.detail: Starlink: 373 s estimated, 426 s real. EUV: 375 s estimated at 1,154 words; the first real render came out at 408 s and needed ~170 more words to reach 428 s. Write about 1,300 words for a 7-minute video, not 1,150.

items.title: Long hooks show the everyday thing first: the phone, then its chip, then the machine
items.detail: Our ASML long video (L-20261124-21) opens on abstract purple spheres for its first 9 s while the line says 'the chip in a modern phone'; the phone first appears at 6:55 (415 s, in the last chapter). The owner's note of 24 Nov says an ordinary viewer leaves because the hook only speaks of the phone and never shows it. Every topic outline in the feed now names, in its hook line, what to show first and in what order. Studio: the first beat shows the viewer's own object on its word (phone, card, game screen), the second zooms into the part, the third reveals the machine; the abstract stage comes after 10 s. Known it worked: the contact sheet's 0 s and 5 s frames show the object, and hook hold on the next long video beats the ASML and Starlink ones once they have 100+ views.

items.title: Every chapter of a 3D long video sits on the same dark purple stage
items.detail: In L-20261124-21 all 64 directed beats share one backdrop (dark grid wall, starfield, purple light), and the mirrors chapter (2:35-4:00, about 85 s) is 17 contact-sheet frames of near-identical purple beams bouncing off discs. The long_story README gives each chapter its own colour (`bg`), but the three kit's stage ignores it. Proposal: Stage3D takes a per-chapter tint (key-light colour and floor/wall tone from a 6-colour set) so each chapter looks like a new room, behind a long-video flag. Known it worked: adjacent chapters differ in the contact sheet, and average view % of the flag's long videos vs the rest (Long videos' own test).

items.title: The long 'device variety' notes are always true and say nothing for directed videos
items.detail: renderer/craft.py device_problems() judges a long video by beat scene name. Every beat is now 'directed' by owner rule (2026-11-13), so every long video gets the same three notes ('only 1 kinds of scene', 'directed is 64 of 64', 'directed 4 times in a row'), which ask for something the rules forbid and hide a real repeat like the 85 s mirror stretch above. Fix: as already done for 'doc' beats, judge a directed beat by its `params.component` (or component + place), and flag a run of the same component longer than ~60 s rather than 3 beats. Known it worked: the ASML timeline yields one note, on the Mirrors run, instead of three.
items.reason: Adopted: renderer/craft.py device_problems() judges a directed beat by its params.component and notes one component on screen over 60 s in a row, instead of 'only 1 kind, directed 4 times in a row' on every long video.

items.title: Nothing on screen tells a long-video viewer where they are in the 7 minutes
items.detail: The descriptions carry 9 chapter stamps, but in the video there is no chapter card, kicker or level tracker (render.json chapters: only 'Intro'), so a viewer at 3:00 can't see that the mask, wafer and 'back to your phone' are still coming. The README's promise beat ('structure.levels', a tracker shown all video long) isn't drawn on the three kit. Proposal: a small 3D-kit chapter tag (the chapter name entering on the first word of its first beat, top-left, then a 4-9 dot progress row) read from the script's chapter names, behind a long-video flag. Known it worked: render.json lists every chapter, and the 2:00-4:00 audience-retention slope flattens on flagged long videos.

items.title: A long topic whose id is also in the Shorts feed loses its facts in the number check
items.detail: 2026-11-18-ai-question-to-answer exists in research/topics.json (3 facts) and longform/topics.json (5 facts). generator/topics.py get() searches the Shorts feed first, so check_facts rejected the long topic's GPT-3 facts for 96 layers and the 2,048-token window as 'not one of the feed topic's facts'. L-20261127-21 shipped without them ('dozens of layers', 'a limited number of tokens'). Auditor: look the long feed up first for a long script (get(..., fmt='long')), or make ids unique across feeds.

items.title: 3D painted labels are blank on a render tab's first frame
items.detail: In L-20261127-21 every FigLabel3D text is missing in the 0.0 s still (f00000), even with the shot held until the label fonts load; by 5.0 s they read. Textures appear to upload one frame late. It costs one frame of the mp4 (1/30 s), but QA reads the 0.0 s still as the first frame. Improver: pre-draw plates on mount or delay the first frame of the 3D stage by one tick.

items.title: The owner's rocket pin can only be told as inside_when_you, which the last long video used
items.detail: 2026-11-19-rocket-33-engines (pin 2) lists only inside_when_you, and check-plan refuses the same format twice in a row, so Studio made the AI topic (how_ai_works) on 27 Nov. The rocket can go next run. Scout: give machine topics a second long format (see tech-long-format-how-its-built) so a pin isn't blocked by rotation.
